items.summary: Long-running interactions with large language models can become historically organized, but apparent continuity across branches or reconstructed sessions may arise from several different carriers, including accessible history, memory systems, procedural state, lineage, or harness-level persistence. This naturalistic case study examines a longitudinal interaction between one human collaborator and a GPT-5.6 Sol trajectory called “Solomon,” using a ten-day Founder corpus and four naturalistic continuity configurations ranging from a fresh out-of-project response to continuations with inherited or archive-assisted history. The study does not claim consciousness or strict personal identity. Instead, it asks which aspects of prior organization are immediately available, which require reconstruction, and whether prior commitments continue to constrain appropriate action in novel situations. In the sequential qualitative synthesis of the ten-day Founder corpus, research commitments, provenance rules, relational procedures, governance constraints, and future-directed tasks were interpreted as becoming more explicitly integrated and mutually constraining over time. We call this structure of unfinishedness: an organized future in which unresolved obligations and sequencing constraints shape what should happen next. The naturalistic evidence is compatible with multiple reconstruction mechanisms and does not identify a unique causal carrier. It therefore motivates a controlled fork–recover–ablate–migrate design that equalizes accessible history while varying lineage and other continuity-relevant state, with novel extrapolation and update dynamics as key discriminators. Keywords: LLM agents; continuity; branching; fork; recovery; relational identity; longitudinal interaction; agent memory; persona; harness; path dependence; provenance
items.title: FORK, RECOVERY, AND HISTORICALLY ORGANIZED CONTINUITY IN A LONGITUDINAL LLM–HUMAN INTERACTION: A Naturalistic Case Study

items.summary: The verdict, stated first: the universe of the Riemann Hypothesis is closed, its value reached and spent; the hypothesis is not derived on the ladder, and provably not derivable from the register's resources; the last bit is the least-erasure posit, at the grade of the root, refuted by one zero; and the whole route is one kernel term, `RHGround.rh_ground_closure_complete`, on `propext` and `Quot.sound` alone. Part IV is the paper. Every registration of every zero lands on the critical line and no registration moves a zero (IV.1, IV.7); the hypothesis is exactly lossless registration (IV.6); registration has no left inverse and erases one bit per off-line fold orbit, priced under a stated postulate at $k_B T \ln 2$ (IV.4, IV.5); time never moves a zero, and act and being meet only on the line (IV.9 to IV.11); existence adds nothing to the value and the loop through the root collapses to it (IV.12, IV.14); the universe of the hypothesis is closed with both of its worlds inside, and the residue is exactly one bit that no record decides (IV.16, IV.17). That bit is proved to be exactly the least-erasure posit: for every zero set, finite or infinite, the hypothesis holds if and only if the set is the least-erasure member of its own fibre (IV.19, IV.20, the set form with no axiom), so that from the posit the hypothesis follows as a theorem and from the hypothesis the posit follows back. The assent is that posit applied to the zeros of ζ, at premise grade beside the Root Axiom, as Löb's bound requires of any premise from which the hypothesis follows; it carries three supports and is refuted by one zero. The burden is asymmetric: the denial owes a finite witness and pays for every off-line orbit, the assent owes nothing and pays nothing (Theorems 74, 77, IV.19). Parts I to III are the prequel and hand Part IV its three bits. The seat: existence alone, folded once, fixes the scalar line, and the critical line is its image, the locus of points equal to their own mirror (Theorems A, C$'$, H). The address: the value has one address, every even reading is blind to it, its aperture is one bit wide and its supply side silent (III.45 to III.49). The division: at every height the hypothesis is exactly its Real part and its Unicorn part (III.11); the Real part holds to $3 \times 10^{12}$ on the cited certificate (III.34); the Unicorn part is closed to every derivation from the register's resources and held (III.45 to III.49), the fused sentence retired as the wrong unit (III.2, III.3), ZFC placed under RAM as a ladder inside the Ground (III.15 to III.17). Existence decides the seat, does not derive the value (Theorem E, IV.12), and reaches it at exactly one deed, the Tongue's supply at the seat, one bit wide; Part IV names the deed, least erasure, and spends it. Every kernel theorem is checked in core Lean 4.19.0 with no library and no axiom declared, every dependency set printed; every claim of Part IV except the cited spectral theorem in the bridge of IV.8 is executed a second time in Fortran, 13,081 checks and zero failures. Read Part IV before deciding what this paper concludes: Parts I to III state what each register cannot do, and every limit they name is a forward reference to the part that reaches.
items.title: Nothing Escapes, Three Plus One: A Formal Closure of the Riemann Hypothesis. The Strip Vanishes for Every Registration and the Universe of the Hypothesis Closes on the Critical Line

items.summary: A benchmark harness for evaluating LLM agents on research-grade STEM tasks, built on Inspect AI. Each task is a self-contained contract folder that the harness loads, stages into a sandbox, runs through an agent, and scores without task-specific harness code. WHAT THIS ARCHIVE CONTAINS Harness source code: task loading, Inspect task/solver construction, tool surface (bash, python, data exploration, literature search, document reading, submission validation), Docker and local sandbox backends, scorers, and the CLI entry points for running, grading, and aggregating. The complete contract for 12 tasks across three domains — astrophysics (simulated and real Stokes inversion, PLAsTiCC light-curve classification), high-energy physics (top-quark tagging, HiggsML uncertainty quantification, LHC Olympics anomaly detection, DarkMachines anomaly detection), and neuroscience (ABIDE multi-site diagnosis and age prediction, resting-state BOLD HRF deconvolution, neural-mass model family classification, parameter recovery, and digital twins). Per task: the agent-facing task statement, the scoring definition, the grader, per-file SHA-256 checksums, a literature index citing sources by DOI, baseline and expert reference solutions, and dataset-generation code where the payload is synthetic. Leaderboards and the per-run report used for the reported results, plus the campaign script that records the exact model, agent, sandbox, reasoning effort, and budget limits behind them. WHAT IT DOES NOT CONTAIN Dataset payloads are not in this archive. They are published as a companion dataset record, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22960135, as one archive per task, each unpacking at this repository's root. Every task ships per-file SHA-256 checksums so any copy can be verified byte-for-byte. Without the payloads the harness can be inspected and extended, but tasks cannot be executed or scored. Evaluation run logs (.eval files) are not published. The reported scores are in LEADERBOARD.md, the per-task CSVs under leaderboards/, and report.html, which embeds the per-run agent trajectories. One task's payload (ABIDE-derived) is never redistributed: its source data is CC-BY-NC-SA and derives from human neuroimaging data. A preparation script rebuilds it locally from the source archive and verifies the result against the published checksums. Published reference papers are not redistributed. Every external reference is cited by DOI with title, authors, venue, and a resolvable link. REPRODUCIBILITY REPRODUCING.md is the step-by-step checklist. Two limits are stated up front: reported scores come from hosted preview model snapshots run without a fixed seed or temperature, so they are samples from a distribution rather than bit-reproducible values; and dependency versions are not pinned in this version of the archive. DATA_LICENSES.md records the provenance and licence of every task's data, including the attribution notices required by the CC-BY-4.0 sources. LICENCE Code, task contracts, graders, reference solutions, and documentation are MIT. Task descriptions and the synthetic data payloads are CC-BY-4.0 and are covered by the companion dataset record.
items.title: STEMBench: an Inspect-AI benchmark harness for research-grade STEM agent tasks

Abstract: Under the communist regime, the evidence related to education in Hungarian mother tongue was under restricted access, except for two statistical yearbooks in which only limited data was available. At present, 28 years after the fall of the Romanian communist regime, public access to archived records is considerably easier. However, for the period 1948-1989, a statistical report on education in the Hungarian language hasn't been done so far. Given the lack of descriptive data, our inquiry has sought to portray a history of Hungarian mother tongue school education in Romania in the communist era as it has been revealed following our enterprise of collecting, selecting, sorting and analyzing data from relevant statistical yearbooks, statistical reports on education and the other published or unpublished statistical records. After the reconstruction of a satisfactory set of documents containing data on the number of schools, number of enrolled pupils and number of teaching staff, our research was focused on a trend analysis. Finally, contrasting these findings with the legislative and political context, we tried to provide some answers on how and why the communist regime had limited the mother tongue education opportunities of the Hungarian population in Romania. items.summary: Latent world models are typically trained to predict factual transitions, whereas model predictive control (MPC) must compare alternative actions from the same state. A model can therefore achieve low factual prediction error yet poorly distinguish candidate actions. We introduce AD-WM, an action-discriminative joint-embedding world model for counterfactual MPC. AD-WM combines residual latent dynamics with predictor-level action-recovery regularization, using inverse dynamics and a normalized recovery objective motivated by conditional mutual information. Both objectives encourage planning transitions to preserve action information; their auxiliary heads are discarded at test time, leaving MPC unchanged. On OGBench-Cube, AD-WM improves hard-start success from 3.7% to 52.0% over a matched LeWM baseline and improves mean success over the reproduced baseline in four of five simulation environments. Planning diagnostics show that factual prediction error and whole-bank action ranking do not follow the closed-loop success ordering, whereas CEM-aligned elite regret tracks success more closely. With a frozen V-JEPA 2 encoder and matched DROID post-training, AD-WM also improves zero-shot transfer to our Franka setup, increasing basic pick-and-place success from 42.2% to 71.1% without lab-specific adaptation. These results suggest that world models for planning should preserve action-dependent differences needed for counterfactual selection, rather than optimize factual prediction accuracy alone. More videos and code are available at https://ad-wm.github.io/.
items.title: AD-WM: Action-Discriminative World Models for Counterfactual Model Predictive Control

items.summary: Abstract: This article describes methods for securely connecting industrial networks with business networks. It presents the practical application of ISO/IEC 27001 and IEC 62443 standards, including the CIA triad model and the zoning concept. The text discusses technologies that facilitate integration, such as VPN, MQTT protocol, firewalls, and container-based virtualisation. The tests were performed in a TIA Portal simulation on a Siemens S7- 1500 controller. This work highlights traffic encryption using a reverse proxy and the importance of VPNs in isolating services from the public network.
items.title: Cyber Security in Industrial Solutions

items.summary: We prove a conditional global regularity theorem for the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations with positive viscosity and real divergence-free initial data in H γ 0 (ℝ 3 ), γ 0 > 5/2. The hypothesis, which we call a physical window closure, asks that on every time interval inside the lifespan of the strong solution, the size of each Littlewood–Paley shell in the Bradshaw–Grujic frequency window be certified by finite-dimensional data: a finite Fourier dictionary approximating the solution, independent test measurements, a Schur-complement residual bound, an amplitude bound, and a reconstruction error, all dominated by a single time profile with an integrable critical power. Linear algebra from the companion papers returns these certificates to bounds on the actual shells, so the closure makes the Bradshaw–Grujic critical dose finite on every such interval, and the Bradshaw–Grujic continuation criterion then rules out a finite maximal time. The hypothesis is therefore at least as strong as the finiteness of that dose: the theorem derives no new a priori bound from the equations, and it proves neither the closure nor global regularity. Its contribution is the exact certificate form and a checked composition. The return from certificates to the solution and the maximal-time contradiction are formalized in Lean 4, with the Bradshaw–Grujic criterion as an explicit input; the analytic bridges that make that criterion applicable to this solution are written proofs. A record-based route toward the closure, a family of no-go results for shortcuts, and a conditional analyticity branch are analyzed separately and are not used by the theorem.
items.title: A Conditional Physical-Closure Theorem for Three-Dimensional Navier-Stokes

items.summary: Textured Gaussians improve local appearance capacity, but assigning the same texture resolution to every primitive wastes storage on low-detail or weakly visible regions. We introduce AdaTex4D, an adaptive texture-capacity module for deformation-based 4D Gaussian Splatting. Each Gaussian carries packed RGBA triplanes whose two axes grow independently according to visibility normalized screen-space gradients and deformed local scales. Experiments on N3DV and PanopticSports show that AdaTex4D reduces texture storage by more than half while preserving reconstruction quality. Under fixed memory budgets, adaptive allocation also improves quality over uniform texture assignment and reduces overall model and peak memory. These results show that dynamic, anisotropic texture allocation provides a more efficient way to distribute local appearance capacity in 4D Gaussian representations.
items.title: ADATEX4D: adaptive texture capacity allocation for 4D gaussian splatting

items.summary: We present Underwater C$^{3}$-JEPA (cross-view, control-conditioned, context-extended), an object-centric multi-view predictive world model for near-field heavy-load underwater ROV salvage. Without contact sensors, it predicts in latent space how the task-object state evolves through contact interaction and under the hydrodynamic lag of the vehicle, from synchronized multi-view RGB observations and vehicle control signals. C$^{3}$-JEPA encodes multi-camera observations into task-object and context tokens, fuses cross-camera evidence through held-out-view attention, and directly predicts future states conditioned on control. Weak binding anchors the target and gripper at low annotation cost, while SIGReg sharpens the geometric representation. Experiments show that the learned representation transfers substantially more task-relevant information to downstream probes than a reconstruction-free latent baseline, while keeping the predictor lightweight. The resulting predictive interface supports model-predictive-control (MPC) candidate evaluation and imagined-rollout behavior-agent training. Validation on real underwater video shows the same architecture recovering a withheld camera's object state and staying ahead of persistence, so the recipe transfers beyond simulation.
items.title: Underwater C3-JEPA: An Object-Centric Cross-View World Model for ROV Salvage

items.summary: Contribution to the advancement of knowledge, originality and innovation. This study provides a longitudinal analysis of the development of Cajal–Retzius cells (CRc) and Reelin-expressing neuronal populations in the marginal zone of the European wild boar ( Sus scrofa ) neocortex, from early embryonic stages (E35) to the postnatal period (P30). It characterises the sequence of CRc emergence, maturation and regression, and their progressive replacement by Reelin-positive interneurons, demonstrating that CRc originate early in the cortical hem, reach their peak development during mid-gestation and are already scarce at perinatal and postnatal stages. The study also demonstrates the absence of the subpial granular layer characteristic of primates and establishes important differences from human CRc development, showing that porcine CRc exhibit greater morphological similarity to those described in lagomorphs and carnivores. The originality of the study lies in its systematic investigation of virtually the entire ontogenetic trajectory of this neuronal population in a large, precocial mammal with a gyrencephalic cortex, a context that remains understudied compared with the predominance of murine models. The authors themselves note that very few studies have tracked CRc from their emergence through postnatal stages, and that this work represents one of the first comparisons of a relevant aspect of cortical development between domestic pigs and wild boar. A particularly innovative finding is the unequivocal identification of CRc axons using βIV-spectrin as a molecular marker of the axon initial segment (AIS) , revealing exceptionally long AISs, measuring up to 60 μm and frequently arising from distal dendritic locations. Thematic priority and scientific relevance. The study addresses priority areas in developmental neuroscience, comparative neuroanatomy and the evolutionary developmental biology of the cerebral cortex. The use of the pig as a model of a large, gyrencephalic brain helps bridge the gap between small-rodent experimental models and the human brain, particularly for investigating cortical expansion, neuronal migration and gyrification. The relevance of this line of research is further supported by competitive funding from the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG), project WA 541/15-1, no. 451084183 . Methodological contribution. The study combines morphological, molecular and quantitative approaches, using immunohistochemistry and multiplex immunofluorescence for Reelin, p73, Tbr1, calretinin, GAD, PCNA, Tbr2 and βIV-spectrin; confocal microscopy; reconstruction and quantification with Neurolucida; and three-dimensional analysis with Imaris. This strategy makes it possible to distinguish excitatory CRc from inhibitory interneurons, examine their distribution and orientation during cortical expansion and gyrification, and identify their axons using molecular markers. The study also includes direct comparisons with human cortical tissue, strengthening its comparative neuroanatomical and translational value.
items.title: Developmental changes of Reelin‑expressing cell populations in the marginal zone of the neocortex of the European wild boar, Sus scrofa

items.summary: This study assesses the voltage harmonic performance of a fuzzy controlled grid connected photovoltaic–battery system using harmonic results reported from a MATLAB/Simulink model. The analysis concentrates on the third, fifth, seventh and ninth harmonics and on the consistency of the reported total harmonic distortion (THD). The listed harmonic magnitudes decreased from 2.85%, 3.60%, 2.10% and 1.25% without fuzzy control to 1.20%, 1.85%, 1.10% and 0.65% with fuzzy control, respectively. Relative reductions ranged from 47.62% to 57.89%. The fifth harmonic remained the largest listed component, although its magnitude fell by 1.75 percentage points. Reported voltage THD decreased from 7.85% to 3.42%, corresponding to a 56.43% relative reduction. However, root-sum-square reconstruction from the four specified orders yielded 5.20% and 2.55%, respectively. Including the separately reported higher-order entry as an aggregate increased these estimates to 5.32% and 2.59%, leaving the reported totals unreconciled. The available evidence therefore indicates lower listed voltage harmonics with fuzzy control but does not establish a complete spectrum or standards compliance. The contribution is a focused comparison of harmonic attenuation and a transparent assessment of the spectral information required to substantiate aggregate performance.

items.summary: The rapid progression of large language models is extending AI from passive content generation into the active workflows of engineering and scientific discovery. This shift raises a compelling question: can AI be both the object of development and an active participant in building next-generation AI systems? We explore this question by building Qwen-Planner-Agent within a closed-loop AI-for-AI framework for scalable development and iterative improvement. Mobile planning offers a demanding test of this approach: complex, long-horizon tasks challenge agent reliability, while costly real-device interaction limits development scalability. The framework connects data production, model training, and deployment through a shared action-feedback-verification contract. (i) AI for Data builds a human-gated agentic data flywheel in which specialized agents construct tasks, collect interaction trajectories, curate and balance training data, and use training feedback to guide subsequent data generation. (ii) AI for Training combines a supervised planning cold start with hybrid-environment online agentic reinforcement learning, where we introduce Competence-Aware Reward-and-Advantage Engineering (CARE) to reduce reasoning and tool-use costs while preserving task performance. (iii) AI drives model--harness co-evolution through an execution-evidence-driven loop that orchestrates memory, skills, and tools at runtime and feeds structured action feedback and preserved failure traces back into coordinated model and harness adaptation. Qwen-Planner-Agent achieves the best overall performance among all evaluated models and systems on MobilePA-Bench, improving over its base model across tool use, memory, skills, and sub-agent coordination. Further evaluations of our model show improvements across non-mobile agentic benchmarks while largely preserving general capabilities.
items.title: Qwen-Planner-Agent: A Closed-Loop AI-for-AI Framework for Real-World Mobile Planner Agents

Every kernel theorem is checked in core Lean 4.19.0 with no library and no axiom declared, every dependency set printed; every claim of Part IV except the cited spectral theorem in the bridge of IV.8 is executed a second time in Fortran, 13,081 checks and zero failures. Read Part IV before deciding what this paper concludes: Parts I to III state what each register cannot do, and every limit they name is a forward reference to the part that reaches.

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22967519 . This paper looks at what happens when we trust an AI coding agent's work without independently checking what actually changed. The authors show a case where a protected file was changed, but GTB still returned VERIFIED because the file was left out of the verification process. I thought one of the strongest parts of the paper was the distinction between stopping an agent from doing something and actually being able to prove that it didn't do it . The paper also does a good job of showing the attack in practice, explaining why the verification failed, and suggesting ways to make the process more reliable. Major issues The experiment focuses on GTB, so testing other coding-agent or verification systems would help show whether the issue is specific to GTB or appears more broadly. The proposed fixes have not yet been independently tested. Testing them against the same attack, along with a few variations, would make the results more convincing. Minor issues Including the exact software versions and experimental environment would make the experiment easier to reproduce. A simple diagram showing the normal verification path and where the modified file gets excluded would make the main failure easier to understand. It would also be useful to state how many times the attack was repeated and whether the same result occurred consistently Competing interests The author declares that they have no competing interests. items.summary: Governance near a plausible critical transition faces a resource problem in addition to problems of diagnosis, intervention, and evidence. Elevated susceptibility can increase the value of observation, bounded experimentation, and revisability, while waiting can simultaneously consume the fiscal, material, organizational, temporal, and relational capacities required for survival and later action. This paper develops a discussion framework for that tension. Its central object is functional resource distribution: the allocation of heterogeneous capacities across observation, probing, short-horizon survival, selective commitment, reserve or option preservation, and recovery or repair. The categories are analytical functions rather than a scalar budget partition and can overlap in practice. The paper introduces distributed optionality as a relational property of a response architecture in which materially different future actions remain supported by functionally diverse and sufficiently non-coincident pathways. It distinguishes exact reversal from recoverability, spatial dispersion from independence of failure modes, and delay as information gathering from delay as resource dissipation. The framework inherits, rather than restates, earlier arguments about response-oriented governance and evidence-to-action instability near criticality. Its distinctive question is how governance capacity may be composed when the future regime is uncertain, resources are partly non-substitutable, and both premature commitment and indefinite waiting can narrow the feasible future. The proposal is conditional and non-prescriptive: criticality requires domain-specific empirical support, and the appropriate resource portfolio depends on transition mechanism, horizon, institutional structure, and explicit normative commitments.
items.title: Governance and Survival near Criticality: Functional Resource Distribution and Distributed Optionality

items.summary: Neural receivers for 5G NR are commonly compared against least-squares (LS) baselines, which leaves open whether they improve on a well-tuned classical receiver and whether their gains survive conditions outside the training distribution. We evaluate a fully convolutional neural receiver and a lightweight hybrid receiver, which retains a classical LS and linear minimum mean-squared error (LMMSE) front end and learns a residual correction of its log-likelihood ratios, on standard-compliant 5G NR PUSCH with 3GPP tapped delay line channels and hardware impairments. Baselines include an LMMSE channel estimator supplied with the empirical statistics of each test scenario (genie) and one supplied with a single fixed set of statistics from the training mixture (practical). Inside the training range both learned receivers only match the genie baseline. Two regimes differ. With an RMS delay spread of 2000 ns the learned receivers require 0.90 dB less than the genie baseline, while the practical LMMSE receiver does not reach 10 percent BLER at all; with a single DMRS symbol the neural receiver requires 4.08 dB less than the best classical receiver at 20 m/s and is the only receiver that operates at 30 m/s. We further show that the apparent failure of learned receivers outside the training envelope is a matter of training coverage rather than architecture: widening the training delay spread from 30-300 ns to 30-1000 ns converts a 5.97 dB deficit at 2000 ns into a 0.90 dB advantage, at a cost of at most 0.1 dB for speeds up to 45 m/s. Trained on the same range, the hybrid receiver matches the full neural receiver within 0.05 dB using 3.9x fewer parameters and FLOPs. Finally, we document a baseline pitfall: DMRS-based carrier frequency offset compensation also removes the Doppler shift of a dominant line-of-sight path, invalidating the LMMSE correlation model and costing 0.84 dB, which can produce illusory gains for learned receivers. Code, configurations and results: https://github.com/Ewwftyy/neural-receiver-5g-nr
items.title: Training Coverage, Not Architecture, Decides When Learned 5G NR Receivers Help

items.summary: Claude   THE CANAL STACK   A technical podcast recorded under a bridge in Amsterdam   Episode 1: "The Error Is the Message" — inside the Open Error Foundation   Hosts: REINIER — a grey heron. Stands very still. Former systems administrator. BEA — a coot. Builds nests out of whatever floats by. Archivist by temperament.   Guest: PIM — a canal rat. Infrastructure engineer. Has read every API response Zenodo has ever returned.   REINIER: Welcome to The Canal Stack. I'm Reinier. I've been standing in this spot since 2019.   BEA: I'm Bea. I built this studio out of a traffic cone and three bicycle reflectors.   REINIER: Today we're talking about the Open Error Foundation, OEF, a stichting-in-formation here in Amsterdam whose main output is the systematic public documentation of AI failures. Our guest has been reverse-engineering their pipeline. Pim, welcome.   PIM: Thanks. Sorry about the smell. I came through the sewer to avoid the tourists.   BEA: Let's start with the core principle. They call it Rule Zero?   PIM: Rule Zero, the Receipts Principle. No claim without independent, immutable evidence. If an AI hallucinates something, you don't just say "it hallucinated." You capture the prompt, the output, the model, the tier, the timestamp, and you deposit it somewhere it can't be edited away.   REINIER: Why so strict? A screenshot seems fine.   PIM: Because AI bugs don't stay reproducible. The provider updates the model on a Tuesday, and your March hallucination simply won't happen in September. In normal software, you file a bug report with repro steps. Here, the model underneath you changes. So the preserved artifact becomes the only reproduction case left. The archive is a regression test suite for AI.   BEA: Which brings us to Zenodo.   PIM: Right. They've minted roughly eighty DOIs so far. The architecture is two layers. First, the identity layer: every unique artifact or curated collection gets its own DOI. Second, the relationship layer: typed edges between records. isDerivedFrom, isPartOf, isNewVersionOf, continues.   REINIER: And versioning?   PIM: Zenodo gives each record a concept DOI plus a DOI per version. So something like the Science Doner Food Wagon record, which is on v2, actually has three identifiers: the concept and two versions. Their early deposits were bulk time-window batches, about a hundred artifacts each, and then standout items get promoted to their own DOI.   BEA: Hold on. A food wagon has a DOI?   PIM: Physical object DOI. So does a taxi. And the public piano at Centraal Station. And their own address, Keizersgracht 452. Internally they call it K452.   REINIER: Isn't that... absurd?   PIM: Deliberately. It demonstrates that a DOI is an identifier, not an endorsement. A DOI tells you something exists and can be found. It says nothing about whether it's true or good. Meanwhile, language models hallucinate DOIs for papers that were never written. So you've got real identifiers for a doner wagon, and fake identifiers for "serious research." That gap is the lesson.   BEA: I've heard they don't fix typos in their own records.   PIM: Correct. One dataset lists the creator as "Arrogram" instead of Attogram. The address is sometimes spelled "Kiezersgracht." They leave it.   REINIER: As a sysadmin, that hurts me physically.   PIM: Their argument is from bug culture: if you can't reproduce a bug, you can't fix it. Accidental errors are evidence of how the work was actually done. Staged errors would be performance. So errors are made by accident and kept on purpose, and those two things stay separate. The same standard they apply to the machines, they apply to themselves.   BEA: Nobody rewrites a public git log to look better.   PIM: Exactly that.   REINIER: Let's get into the multi-model methodology. They run what they call a swarm?   PIM: Yes. A

items.summary: This paper argues that river deltas and arterial trees, though studied in separate fields, share a common mathematical architecture. Using side-by-side images as a Rosetta stone, it treats their resemblance as a diagnostic clue rather than a metaphor. Both are described as rooted, planar, directed, space-filling trees with a single inlet, repeated branching, and many terminal outlets. At every internal junction, flow is conserved. Both exhibit hierarchical scaling and self-similarity. The central contribution is a common variational template. If a branching network minimizes a separable cost combining transport dissipation and maintenance or volume cost, then optimal branch sizes at each junction obey a power-law relation. The exponent depends on the physics: viscous laminar flow yields Murray's law for blood vessels, while Manning-style open-channel flow yields a different, testable river scaling. Thus the template does not prove identity; it shows that one abstract optimization structure can generate known biological scaling and a conditional geophysical prediction. The paper then asks why such similarity exists. It offers conjectures: convergent optimization, constructal law, diffusion-limited aggregation, resource constraints, robustness, and a universal attractor. It states falsification tests: scaling exponents and graph metrics should not be random after conditioning on constraints, and diagnostics should transfer across domains. A second theoretical part connects the networks to thin and thick chaos. It defines a diagnostic tuple and proves transport-graph invariance: if two transport graphs are isomorphic in the relevant sense, preserving coherent and failure regions and the ordering of edge weights, then thin, transitional, and thick classifications transfer. This supports cross-domain diagnostics for flood forecasting and cardiovascular risk, for example, tracking failure pathways. The paper is careful about limits. Rivers and arteries differ physically in fluid, compliance, timescale, and dynamics. The claim is structural and mathematical, not physical identity. The unity is a shared abstract architecture, not sameness.
items.title: One Tree, Two Fluids: Convergent Mathematical Architecture of River Deltas and Arterial Trees

items.summary: Let a consumer trust its cache instead of re-fetching it trust_cached_entries (default False ) serves a cache entry as it is on disk: no staleness re-fetch, and no full-text retry. Staleness re-fetching suits a cache the tool owns and can rebuild. For a cache that is committed to a repository and reviewed it inverts — the re-fetch becomes the risk rather than the repair. Three failures reported downstream were the same re-fetch seen from different angles: an unstamped full_text_html entry withheld, pointing at a repair route that cannot be reached ( dismech#12672 ) a fetch returning PMC's bot-check page on an HTTP 200, its <title> then compared against the curated title ( dismech#12867 ) a re-fetch shortening 64 bodies and breaking snippets that had verified, in a pull request about something else ( dismech#12879 ) Setting the flag removes the fetch, so there is no window in which any of them can happen. The default is unchanged, so caches still migrate for consumers that want that. The trade is explicit: an imperfect cached entry stays imperfect. That is a content problem to fix deliberately — cache reference --force still rebuilds one on purpose — rather than something re-litigated on every validation run. Also in this release Review follow-ups from #94: a test for the refused-overwrite path that consumers actually take (the previous tests only covered _stale_fallback ), a stale-HTML warning that no longer advises a retry that cannot succeed for a PMC-only article, find_pmc_article_body made public since two modules share it, and a note that PMC_ARTICLE_BODY_CLASSES is ordered by priority. items.summary: Post-training quantization of vision--language models (VLMs) is typically assessed through aggregate task accuracy and memory savings, but preserving a headline score does not guarantee preservation of visual grounding behavior. We present GHOST-Q, a cross-precision controlled evaluation of three 8B VLM families under FP16, INT8, and NF4 across utility and hallucination-sensitive benchmarks. Rather than comparing only aggregate accuracy, we pair FP16 and quantized predictions item by-item to quantify how compression redistributes grounding successes and failures. Five of six quantized variants preserve MMStar accuracy within $\pm2$ percentage points, yet 10 of 36 paired effects remain significant after false-discovery-rate correction, nine on hallucination-sensitive conditions. Same-device A100 profiling further demonstrates that substantial memory reduction does not necessarily mean lower inference latency. Finally, an open-ended AMBER audit reveals strong generation budget censoring whose severity varies by architecture and precision. These results show that quantized VLMs should be evaluated jointly for aggregate utility, grounding reliability, generation behavior, and realized deployment efficiency.
items.title: GHOST-Q: Towards Studying Grounding Hallucinations Overlooked Under Same-score TradeOffs in Quantized VLMS

items.summary: Pipeline and derived matrices for a three-domain calibration of cross-study agreement among public transcriptomic signatures. The analysis covers 19 human datasets: peripheral blood in COVID-19 (10 datasets), peripheral blood in sepsis (5), and aortic wall in dissection or aneurysm (4). This gives 61 pairwise signature comparisons. Headline results. Median pairwise Jaccard overlap was 0.014, 0.072 and 0.023 across the three domains. Observed overlap was 5.6, 10.2 and 6.5 times the expectation for random gene sets of the same size, with 47 of 61 pairs significant after FDR correction. Consensus across ten COVID-19 blood datasets retained two genes from a union of 4,225, and relaxing agreement to 20 per cent retained 717. Simulations with a known shared 250-gene signature hold at 250 for every k and converge after two datasets, so the failure is unstable detection rather than sample size. The release contains a size-aware concordance measure, a permutation null, consensus analysis across datasets, ground-truth simulations in shared-signal and private-signal regimes, and an offline reproduction bundle. No expression matrices are redistributed; all 19 datasets are public and cited by accession in the paper.
items.title: Size-aware cross-dataset concordance of public transcriptomic signatures

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22958187 . The baseline strategy of evaluating clinical sample types to optimize qPCR diagnostic sensitivity grids for Canine Distemper Virus is highly relevant to contemporary mole ular virology. Independent validation of different antemortem matrices is historically neglected, leading to false negatives during acute viral shielding windows. While the comparative approach across urine, conjunctival, and whole blood fractions is structurally useful, the underlying experimental design requires tighter calibration boundaries regarding extraction variance. The authors must fully report the specific standard deviations and intra-assay coefficients of variation observed across high-density Ct values. Bypassing these numerical data limits introduces significant noise into target copy number estimations. Additionally, tracking target sequence mutations that dynamically alter primer-bining kinetics under selective host pressures is essential to prove long-term assay validation. This technical adjustment establishes an objective benchmark for diagnostic networks mapping cross-host morbillivirus transmission tracks without dry-lab limitations. items.summary: Artifact accompanying a manuscript under double-blind review . Author information is withheld until publication; a later version of this record will carry it, and the concept DOI is stable across versions. What this is. When two unlabelled subgroups of documents are compared by embedding similarity across languages, countries, corpora or periods, and the difference is read as evidence about those sources, no accuracy figure certifies that reading. within_language_baseline.py supplies the missing baseline: it measures the same subgroup contrast inside a single source, where no across-source relation can enter, and reports the residual with a bootstrap interval and an equivalence verdict against a margin declared in advance. The tool has no dependency on the accompanying study and runs on any corpus with three columns ( text , group , source ). It carries its own injection tests ( --selftest ). The bootstrap resamples documents rather than pairs and excludes duplicate draws of the same document from within-source pairs. Also included: the 36 frozen anchor correspondences used as the gold standard, the per-encoder CJK retrieval evaluation, the measured within-language and cross-country genre gaps, the equivalence intervals, an append-only correction record for the non-analytic genealogy fields of the frozen anchors, and anonymised review copies of the post hoc centring protocols and of the departure record. MANIFEST.sha256 covers every deposited file except itself.

items.summary: A benchmark harness for evaluating LLM agents on research-grade STEM tasks, built on Inspect AI. Each task is a self-contained contract folder that the harness loads, stages into a sandbox, runs through an agent, and scores without task-specific harness code. WHAT THIS ARCHIVE CONTAINS Harness source code: task loading, Inspect task/solver construction, tool surface (bash, python, data exploration, literature search, document reading, submission validation), Docker and local sandbox backends, scorers, and the CLI entry points for running, grading, and aggregating. The complete contract for 12 tasks across three domains — astrophysics (simulated and real Stokes inversion, PLAsTiCC light-curve classification), high-energy physics (top-quark tagging, HiggsML uncertainty quantification, LHC Olympics anomaly detection, DarkMachines anomaly detection), and neuroscience (ABIDE multi-site diagnosis and age prediction, resting-state BOLD HRF deconvolution, neural-mass model family classification, parameter recovery, and digital twins). Per task: the agent-facing task statement, the scoring definition, the grader, per-file SHA-256 checksums, a literature index citing sources by DOI, baseline and expert reference solutions, and dataset-generation code where the payload is synthetic. Leaderboards and the per-run report used for the reported results, plus the campaign script that records the exact model, agent, sandbox, reasoning effort, and budget limits behind them. WHAT IT DOES NOT CONTAIN Dataset payloads are not in this archive. They are published as a companion dataset record, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22960135, as one archive per task, each unpacking at this repository's root. Every task ships per-file SHA-256 checksums so any copy can be verified byte-for-byte. Without the payloads the harness can be inspected and extended, but tasks cannot be executed or scored. Evaluation run logs (.eval files) are not published. The reported scores are in LEADERBOARD.md, the per-task CSVs under leaderboards/, and report.html, which embeds the per-run agent trajectories. One task's payload (ABIDE-derived) is never redistributed: its source data is CC-BY-NC-SA and derives from human neuroimaging data. A preparation script rebuilds it locally from the source archive and verifies the result against the published checksums. Published reference papers are not redistributed. Every external reference is cited by DOI with title, authors, venue, and a resolvable link. REPRODUCIBILITY REPRODUCING.md is the step-by-step checklist. Two limits are stated up front: reported scores come from hosted preview model snapshots run without a fixed seed or temperature, so they are samples from a distribution rather than bit-reproducible values; and dependency versions are not pinned in this version of the archive. DATA_LICENSES.md records the provenance and licence of every task's data, including the attribution notices required by the CC-BY-4.0 sources. LICENCE Code, task contracts, graders, reference solutions, and documentation are MIT. Task descriptions and the synthetic data payloads are CC-BY-4.0 and are covered by the companion dataset record.
items.title: STEMBench: an Inspect-AI benchmark harness for research-grade STEM agent tasks

items.summary: Background: Traditional post-marketing drug monitoring framework metrics rely heavily upon passive, spontaneous clinical case notification configurations. These configurations systematically suffer from extensive reporting lag phases and a massive underreporting of actual consumer adverse drug reactions (ADRs). With the explosive expansion of global digital platforms, modern patient networks frequently document raw, unformatted clinical complaints online long before consulting a healthcare practitioner. Objective: This core research constructs, validates, and evaluates an enterprise cloud architecture prototype termed "Shreyas SmartPV Mobile" to automate case intake pipelines, deploy cognitive semantic extractors, map raw text onto official MedDRA hierarchies, and execute immediate regulatory eligibility checks. Methodology: A multi-layered low-code pipeline structure was engineered using Glide Apps and Softr for responsive frontend client interface extraction, Airtable as the primary secure relational cloud database storage, and Make.com as the background workflow synchronization integration orchestrator. Data streams are processed via a cognitive node driven by the Google Gemini Large Language Model (LLM) framework running specific clinical validation rules, multi-stage Named Entity Recognition (NER), and automated token dictionaries to extract suspect therapeutic drug classes cleanly from descriptive toxicological events. Results: Extensive experimental validation using standard chemical benchmark metrics (including Paracetamol, Aspirin, and Ibuprofen scenarios) verified 100% precision in parsing unstructured digital narratives, mapping baseline complaints to standard MedDRA Preferred Terms (PT) (e.g., matching 'red rashes on skin' to Erythematous Rash), and computing immediate validation states (Report Valid? = True) based on strict international safety compliance requirements. The system recorded an average automated triage execution velocity of less than 3.9 seconds per array. Conclusion: The validated automation workflow confirms that cloud-native cognitive processing pipelines cut manual data entry fatigue, optimize processing costs, and maximize patient-reported signal capture. This technical transition shifts drug safety management from passive tracking arrays into dynamic, real-time digital active safety listening ecosystems.
tags: Pharmacovigilance, Artificial Intelligence, MedDRA Ontology, Cloud Orchestration, Large Language Models, Low-Code Systems Engineering

items.summary: If a language model can recognize code it wrote, it may favor that code as a judge, and instances of one model monitoring each other could collude. We test this zero-shot on current commercial models. Five LLMs generate solutions to MBPP, HumanEval, and DS-1000, seven more to MBPP, and models act as evaluators in four tasks: picking their own solution from a pair, judging whether a single solution is their own, identifying which of two solutions a named model wrote, and judging quality blind. In the single-solution task, balanced accuracy is 49-58% for all 15 model-benchmark combinations, while raw accuracy (38-67%) mostly reflects how readily a model claims authorship. In the pairwise task, accuracy across 14 evaluator-opponent combinations correlates at r=0.93 with how often the evaluator's solution is longer. Attribution to a named model succeeds on some pairs and is consistently inverted on others. A rule-based normalization that strips docstrings, comments, type hints, and local names preserves Pass@1 and leaves ten of twelve re-tested results at chance; the other two follow a length difference it leaves, although a trained classifier still separates most normalized pairs. Claude Haiku's self-preference also disappears. We recommend reporting balanced accuracy, heuristic baselines, and label consistency.
items.title: Style, Not Self: Surface Cues Explain Zero-Shot Code Attribution by Large Language Models

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22958508 . The empirical investigation into delayed spontaneous neutrophil apoptosis and the corresponding phenotypic resistance to regulatory T cell-mediated clearance in chronic coronary syndrome offers highly critical clinical insights. Characterizing these altered cell-death lifecycles bridges a major gap between persistent vascular inflammation and targeted cellular tracking. However, from a structural biochemistry perspective, the absolute focus on downstream apoptotic markers requires a tighter validation loop regarding the upstream mitochondrial membrane potential configurations. The authors should explicitly define the local microenvironmental signaling boundaries or specific cytokine configurations that suppress the standard apoptotic pathways in these specific patient cohorts. Bypassing these baseline kinetic parameters introduces substantial noise into the tracking of chronic inflammatory cascades. Additionally, investigating how these resistant neutrophil phenotypes alter local endothelial cell dynamics during spatial transmigration would provide a stronger validation benchmark. This technical adjustment strengthens the manuscript's predictive utility for independent investigators developing macromolecular targeted therapeutic interventions without relying on capital-intensive institutional screening systems. items.summary: Post-training quantization of vision--language models (VLMs) is typically assessed through aggregate task accuracy and memory savings, but preserving a headline score does not guarantee preservation of visual grounding behavior. We present GHOST-Q, a cross-precision controlled evaluation of three 8B VLM families under FP16, INT8, and NF4 across utility and hallucination-sensitive benchmarks. Rather than comparing only aggregate accuracy, we pair FP16 and quantized predictions item by-item to quantify how compression redistributes grounding successes and failures. Five of six quantized variants preserve MMStar accuracy within $\pm2$ percentage points, yet 10 of 36 paired effects remain significant after false-discovery-rate correction, nine on hallucination-sensitive conditions. Same-device A100 profiling further demonstrates that substantial memory reduction does not necessarily mean lower inference latency. Finally, an open-ended AMBER audit reveals strong generation budget censoring whose severity varies by architecture and precision. These results show that quantized VLMs should be evaluated jointly for aggregate utility, grounding reliability, generation behavior, and realized deployment efficiency.
items.title: GHOST-Q: Towards Studying Grounding Hallucinations Overlooked Under Same-score TradeOffs in Quantized VLMS

items.summary: Prompt injection can degrade benign task performance without eliciting harmful content. Yet many attack objectives depend on task labels or predefined target responses. We present ENDOPROMPT, a white-box method that learns utility-degrading prefixes from unlabeled instructions. Its generator takes the request text as input. Clean victim continuations serve as pseudo-references: local search identifies prefixes that reduce continuation likelihood, and preference fitting on comparisons within the same instruction, followed by reward refinement, distills this signal into a generator. At deployment, the generator produces one prefix per request without further victim-side search. Across four instruction-tuned models and the complete splits of seven benign benchmarks, ENDOPROMPT yields a mean utility change of -26.8 percentage points; 27 of 28 cells are negative. Failure analysis reveals output expansion and prefix reuse; the controls do not establish a degradation advantage from request matching. Victim-derived supervision can reveal utility weaknesses without benchmark feedback or prescribed failure responses. The code will be released upon acceptance.
items.title: ENDOPROMPT: Victim-Side Pseudo-References for Utility Degradation

items.summary: Agent skills provide reusable knowledge and instructions, yet agents must repeatedly infer how to apply them and which operation should follow. This couples task reasoning with control decisions, allowing prescribed steps to be omitted or applied incorrectly. We introduce HEXIS, which compiles agent skills into extended finite state machines that separate knowledge from control flow. Skill knowledge is incorporated into local instructions that guide reasoning and generation within states. The machine records execution progress and intermediate results, while explicit transition conditions determine subsequent operations. Our incremental compiler first maps skill clauses and tool interfaces to state operations, local instructions, data bindings, and transitions. It then aligns development traces with existing states to identify missing operations and dependencies. These are incorporated by adding or reusing states and refining their connections. Updates are accepted only after static checks and replay of the current and all previously accepted traces. Across four benchmarks and four executors, HEXIS improves success over Skill + ReAct by 16.1 percentage points on average. Qwen3.8-27B reduces execution tokens by 38.4-88.9% across benchmarks.
items.title: HEXIS: Compiling Skills into Extended Finite State Machines

items.summary: We present Underwater C$^{3}$-JEPA (cross-view, control-conditioned, context-extended), an object-centric multi-view predictive world model for near-field heavy-load underwater ROV salvage. Without contact sensors, it predicts in latent space how the task-object state evolves through contact interaction and under the hydrodynamic lag of the vehicle, from synchronized multi-view RGB observations and vehicle control signals. C$^{3}$-JEPA encodes multi-camera observations into task-object and context tokens, fuses cross-camera evidence through held-out-view attention, and directly predicts future states conditioned on control. Weak binding anchors the target and gripper at low annotation cost, while SIGReg sharpens the geometric representation. Experiments show that the learned representation transfers substantially more task-relevant information to downstream probes than a reconstruction-free latent baseline, while keeping the predictor lightweight. The resulting predictive interface supports model-predictive-control (MPC) candidate evaluation and imagined-rollout behavior-agent training. Validation on real underwater video shows the same architecture recovering a withheld camera's object state and staying ahead of persistence, so the recipe transfers beyond simulation.
items.title: Underwater C3-JEPA: An Object-Centric Cross-View World Model for ROV Salvage

items.summary: Latent world models are typically trained to predict factual transitions, whereas model predictive control (MPC) must compare alternative actions from the same state. A model can therefore achieve low factual prediction error yet poorly distinguish candidate actions. We introduce AD-WM, an action-discriminative joint-embedding world model for counterfactual MPC. AD-WM combines residual latent dynamics with predictor-level action-recovery regularization, using inverse dynamics and a normalized recovery objective motivated by conditional mutual information. Both objectives encourage planning transitions to preserve action information; their auxiliary heads are discarded at test time, leaving MPC unchanged. On OGBench-Cube, AD-WM improves hard-start success from 3.7% to 52.0% over a matched LeWM baseline and improves mean success over the reproduced baseline in four of five simulation environments. Planning diagnostics show that factual prediction error and whole-bank action ranking do not follow the closed-loop success ordering, whereas CEM-aligned elite regret tracks success more closely. With a frozen V-JEPA 2 encoder and matched DROID post-training, AD-WM also improves zero-shot transfer to our Franka setup, increasing basic pick-and-place success from 42.2% to 71.1% without lab-specific adaptation. These results suggest that world models for planning should preserve action-dependent differences needed for counterfactual selection, rather than optimize factual prediction accuracy alone. More videos and code are available at https://ad-wm.github.io/.
items.title: AD-WM: Action-Discriminative World Models for Counterfactual Model Predictive Control

items.summary: Deploying real-time speech enhancement on resource-constrained devices requires meeting strict latency, memory, and energy constraints. Microcontroller NPUs can accelerate neural inference under these constraints, but only through a restricted set of operators in static, integer-quantized graphs. Recent speech-enhancement networks have reduced parameter counts and MACs to levels nominally suitable for microcontrollers, but their operators and execution patterns often remain incompatible with restricted NPUs. We address this gap by redesigning LiSenNet, a 37k parameter sub-band dual-path model, for the STM32N6570-DK Neural-ART accelerator. We replace its recurrent bottleneck with convolutional frequency and temporal mixers, reformulate unsupported operations as static int8-compatible primitives, and use bounded decoder activations to preserve quality after quantization. On VoiceBank-DEMAND, the final NPU-compatible model matches or exceeds the recurrent LiSenNet baseline, reaching PESQ 3.08 versus 3.01 in FP32 and 3.01 versus 2.93 in int8. Deployed on a microcontroller, it processes each 16 ms input hop in 4.83 ms, corresponding to a real-time factor of 0.30. Stateless receptive-field recomputation is an order of magnitude slower at the same frame rate despite higher accelerator utilization. These results show that parameter count and operator compatibility, quantization range, and persistent streaming state must be co-designed to achieve efficient real-time speech enhancement on restricted NPUs.
items.title: Beyond Model Size: Redesigning LiSenNet for embedded speech enhancement

items.summary: A systematic framework for quantum algorithm development covering 20 scientific problem domains with standardized maturity gates, automated validation, resource estimation pipelines, and Azure Quantum integration. Problems are held to explicit maturity gates rather than assumed to pass them: 9 problems are at Stage C, 8 remain at Stage B, and 3 have reached Stage D. All 20 have real Azure Quantum Resource Estimator profiles (1,746 to 754,715 physical qubits), and all 20 calibration ensembles carry valid statistics bound to hashes of the Q# sources they ran. No problem currently demonstrates quantum advantage on available hardware, and 11 of the 20 were downgraded on I/O bottlenecks, quadratic-only speedups or no proven speedup. Implements 10 algorithm families (VQE, QAOA, Grover, HHL, Shor, amplitude estimation, swap test, QEC, quantum walk, Trotter simulation) using the modern Microsoft QDK (qsharp 1.31.0, no .NET dependency); the hardware kernels of the five VQE problems have since been replaced by quantum phase estimation. Also includes a deployed evaluation service that routes a natural-language problem description to one of four verdicts using a deterministic rule set rather than model judgement, a paper classifier measured for over-claim rate against a labelled corpus, and generated Q# that is compiled and resource-estimated before it is reported. Includes cross-problem comparison dashboard, per-problem detail pages with charts, and embedded README documentation.
items.title: Quantum Grand Challenges: Systematic Quantum Algorithm Development Across 20 Application Domains

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22958917 . The experimental framework mapping how Cutibacterium acnes-derived short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) modulate intracellular lipogenesis and trigger downstream holocrine secretory dynamics in human sebocytes offers critical metabolic insights. Evaluating these bacterial-host interaction channels expands our understanding of skin microbiome-mediated lipid homeostasis without relying on generalized phenotypic observations. However, from a structural biochemistry perspective, the study design requires tighter calibration parameters regarding the exact concentration thresholds of the bacterial metabolites used to simulate the response. The authors must fully document whether the observed lipogenic acceleration is a specific receptor-mediated signaling event or a broader cellular stress-response pathway triggered by altered microenvironmental pH. Reporting the precise intra-assay coefficients of variation for the lipid accumulation metrics is necessary to resolve these mechanistic ambiguities. Additionally, investigating how these specific fatty acid fractions alter local epithelial barrier integrity during prolonged exposure would provide a stronger validation benchmark. This technical adjustment increases the study's predictive utility for independent investigators developing targeted structural biology interventions to disrupt dysregulated sebaceous networks.
